verdicts.reason: A leaves ~150px of dead space on the left while the SOLSTICE logo is shrunk to an illegible wordmark and jammed into the top-right corner over a bubble; the subtitle is tiny and the can is crowded up against the copy. B puts brand, then message, then product in a clear left-to-right line with a strong headline and readable subtitle, but the logo is small, its wordmark spacing is uneven ('SOLSTIC E'), and the can is cramped at the right edge with an unreadable label.

A is a balanced banner with the can on the left, a large headline, a readable subtitle on one shared left edge, and the logo given room on the right. It only needs polish: the can sits tight to the top and its label is illegible. B has the same flaws as pair 1 A: a big empty left zone, an undersized subtitle, a tiny logo crammed into the corner and a can squeezed against the text block.

A has an unbalanced empty left third, a tiny corner logo and a weak subtitle. B's headline and subtitle run almost flush against the left canvas edge with no margin. B's logo floats mid-canvas with its sun detached, and the wordmark looks clipped ('SOLSTICL'), damaging the brand. B also crams the can into the right edge. That edge violation and broken logo make B slightly worse despite its larger type.
